audion.title: Audion: Turning a LinkedIn Click into a Lead
audion.subtitle: For Audion's US launch, I designed the landing page for its LinkedIn campaign, covering design, copywriting and Webflow implementation.
audion.team: Project Manager, SEO, Paid Search, Tracking
audion.contextP1a: Audion, an AI-powered audio advertising platform, was launching in the US with a LinkedIn ad campaign targeting CMOs. The offer: a 22-page white paper, the
audion.contextP1b: , exploring how US media budgets are allocated. My mission was to design the landing page visitors reached after clicking the ads and turn that traffic into qualified leads. I worked exclusively on this campaign page, not on Audion's main website.
audion.contextP2: I received the brief from the project manager and worked with the SEO, paid search and tracking teams. I also validated decisions with Audion's CMOs and sales team.
audion.challenge1Text: Most LinkedIn users browse on their phones, so the page had to be designed for mobile first.
audion.challenge2Text: After clicking an ad, visitors need to see the creative's promise reinforced within seconds.
audion.challenge3Text: Convince CMOs to share their contact details for a brand that was still relatively unknown in the US.
audion.challenge4Text: Prioritise lead generation while introducing Audion to visitors who land on the page.
audion.strategy1Text: Generate qualified leads through the form, then introduce Audion to visitors who land on the page.
audion.strategy2Text: A hero section focused on the white paper and form, followed by a content preview, social proof and an introduction to Audion.
audion.strategy3Text: A hero section combining the value proposition and form, followed by an 'Why audio?' section and a more detailed introduction to Audion.
audion.strategyConclusion: The final page follows Version A's structure, with an additional section on the benefits of audio drawn from Version B.
audion.decision1Text: The sales team wanted five fields to collect as much data as possible. I recommended limiting the form to two or three fields, as each additional field can reduce completion rates, especially on mobile. The final form has three fields: name, role (advertiser, agency or adtech) and work email.
audion.decision2Title: A hero section built to drive downloads
audion.decision2Text: Above the fold: a benefit-led headline, a visual of the report, a '22 pages' label, brand logos to build trust and the form.
audion.decision3Title: A thank-you page that extends the journey
audion.decision3Text: A download confirmation, followed by a call to action for Audion and three cards inviting visitors to explore further.
audion.decision4Text: There was no user testing on this project. I refined the page using my landing page experience and feedback from the sales team and CMOs. Iterations focused on the form, visuals, headline and copy, icons, logos and buttons.
audion.resultsText: The landing page was delivered and launched within six weeks, serving as the destination for LinkedIn ads. It sat at the bottom of the funnel, and traffic remained limited, so I don't have reliable conversion data to share.
audion.takeawaysText: Presenting two versions made the discussion more concrete. When discussing the form, framing the conversation around leads and completion rates helped me get buy-in from the sales team. My marketing background proved useful.
audion.nextStepsText: Test two headlines and two form lengths, then analyse mobile sessions to identify where visitors drop off.
riseup.heroSubtitle: Rise Up is a B2B learning platform that uses AI to personalize learning experiences. The goal was to redesign the marketing website to better reflect this positioning and modernize the brand image. I designed the new interfaces, created the mockups and prototype, and handed them off to developers for implementation in HubSpot.
riseup.testimonial: Camille is an outstanding UX/UI designer who makes the complex process of a website or app redesign feel easy! We collaborated on the rebuild of the Rise Up website, transforming it into both a brand showcase for a learning tech innovator and a powerful demand-generation engine. She was deeply committed to realising our vision, constantly challenging assumptions, and introducing fresh ideas to keep the site aligned with evolving trends. Thanks to her expertise and drive, we delivered on time and with a result we're proud of.
riseup.overviewText: Rise Up was expanding internationally and needed a marketing website that clearly communicated its value to a global audience of HR managers, L&D leaders, and digital learning managers. The existing website wasn't supporting this growth. It lacked clarity, scalability, and a strong user experience, creating friction for both prospective clients and internal teams.
riseup.audit1Text: Visitors struggled to quickly understand Rise Up's unique selling points (USPs).
riseup.audit2Text: Content was buried under a confusing structure, making it hard to find relevant information.
riseup.audit3Text: Pricing and feature details weren't clearly presented, creating distrust.
riseup.audit4Text: The site had to work seamlessly within HubSpot, limiting layout and interaction options.
riseup.audit5Text: No digital design system existed, leading to inconsistent brand representation across marketing materials.
riseup.research1Text: I spoke directly with existing clients and prospects across French and UK markets to understand their perspective on Rise Up and the broader LMS landscape.
riseup.research2Text: Interviewed Rise Up's leadership team (CEO, CTO, Head of Learning, Sales & Marketing) to align on business objectives and gather internal insights on the website's current challenges.
riseup.research3Text: Analyzed the UX and UI of main competitor websites to benchmark industry standards, best practices and where Rise Up could stand out.
riseup.solution1Text: Simplified and restructured the navigation menu to ensure clear hierarchies and intuitive categories.
riseup.solution2Text: Introduced clearer pricing visibility, transparent messaging, and highlighted social proof elements.
riseup.solution3Text: Developed a scalable UI system with reusable components, typography rules, and a cohesive color palette aligned with Rise Up's new branding.
riseup.solution4Text: Restructured the content and interactions to create a smoother flow, guiding visitors logically from learning about the platform to requesting a demo.
riseup.solution5Text: Worked on bringing unique selling points to the forefront with dedicated sections, bold typography, and engaging visuals.
riseup.resultsText: After launch, initial feedback from both Rise Up's internal teams and clients confirmed that the redesign achieved its goals: easier to communicate product value to prospects, simpler navigation for L&D managers to find relevant content, and improved trust due to transparent pricing and feature clarity.
riseup.nextStepsIntro: The website redesign was only the first step in Rise Up's digital transformation. To help them fully leverage the new design, I continued working with the team on two strategic missions:
riseup.creativeProductionText: Designed static visuals and 2D animated videos to elevate the website experience and support marketing campaigns. These assets aligned closely with the new brand and helped communicate Rise Up's innovative features more dynamically.
riseup.designGuideText: Developed a clear, actionable Website Design Guide for marketing and web teams. This resource ensures the site remains user-friendly, consistent, and optimized, even as new content and pages are added.
